findings.title: Silence drawer never opens in the new list view: clicking 'Silence notifications' does nothing
findings.body: RuleActionsButtons now supports being called with only a promRule (no rulerRule), which is exactly how GrafanaRuleListItem uses it in the new ruler-less list view. In AlertRuleMenu the Silence menu item is shown based on the new prom-rule abilities (useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns Silence=[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]), so for a Grafana alerting rule the 'Silence notifications' item is visible and clickable (the updated GrafanaGroupLoader test even asserts its presence). However, clicking it only calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true), and the drawer itself is still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the (now optional) rulerRule. With rulerRule undefined the drawer is never rendered, so the silence action silently does nothing. The drawer needs to be renderable from the prom rule (e.g. a prom-based silence drawer) or the menu item must be hidden when no rulerRule is available.

findings.title: skipToken path returns enabled abilities, granting Duplicate on cloud rules based on Grafana permissions
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbility translate skipToken into `undefined` and call useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). With rule undefined, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, isPluginProvided/isProvisioned are false, and the abilities are computed with getRulesPermissions('grafana'): Duplicate becomes [true, ctx.hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]. AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken whenever promRule is not a Grafana prom rule (i.e. for every cloud/Mimir rule), and computes canDuplicate as ruler || grafana. As a result a user who has the Grafana-managed rule create permission but NOT AlertingRuleExternalWrite will now see the Duplicate menu item on cloud rules (previously only the ruler-based ability, which checks the external-write permission for that data source, was used). The skipToken/undefined-rule path should yield all-disabled abilities instead of permission-evaluated ones.

findings.title: Federated rule groups lose their immutable treatment after useAllAlertRuleAbilities refactor
findings.body: Before this change, useAllAlertRuleAbilities (still used via useAlertRuleAbility by CombinedRule consumers such as the existing RulesTable) computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Update/Delete/Pause unsupported for federated (cross-tenant) Mimir/GEM rule groups. The hook now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only receives a RulerRuleDTO and hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. Consequently, for rules in federated groups the Edit/Delete/Pause abilities become 'supported' again and the corresponding buttons/menu items reappear; attempting the operation will fail against the ruler or, worse, modify a group the UI intentionally treated as immutable. The federated check needs to be preserved somewhere in the new delegation chain.

findings.title: Export (and Pause) abilities restricted to alerting rules, recording rules lose Export in list view
findings.body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, ModifyExport is computed as [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed] where isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). The ruler-based equivalent uses isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), which matches both Grafana alerting AND recording rules, so recording rules currently expose the 'Export / With modifications' menu item (the modify-export flow supports recording rules). In the new ruler-less list view the rulerRule is absent, so canExport relies solely on the prom-based ability and recording rules lose the Export menu entry. The same narrowing applies to Pause/Restore (Grafana recording rules are pausable, but the prom-based ability requires an alerting rule), which will bite once the pause menu item is wired to prom rules.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without React key in the filtered rule list
findings.body: In FilterViewResults the rules are rendered via rules.map(...). The previous code rendered <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>, and the 'datasource' and 'default' branches still pass key={key}, but the 'grafana' branch now renders <GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={...} ... /> with no key prop. This triggers React's missing-key warning and forces index-based reconciliation for Grafana rows; since these rows contain stateful children (AlertRuleMenu, silence drawer state, delete modal), any future reorder/removal of rows could attach that state to the wrong rule. Pass key={key} as before.

findings.title: Rule link no longer carries the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem (in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the rule href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail view returned the user to the originating (possibly filtered) rule list. The new component builds `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo, so the detail view's back navigation falls back to the default alert list and loses the user's list context/filters. Re-add the returnTo parameter.

findings.title: Stale comment about preloading ruler rules after ruler prefetch was removed
findings.body: The diff removes the alertRuleApi prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...) dispatch but leaves the comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX. Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded' and the variable name cacheAndRulerPreload. The comment now describes behavior that no longer exists and is misleading about what the remaining upsertQueryData does; update the comment and rename the variable.
